samples.summary: The canonical image-editing design doc's image-selection keyboard table was not updated for the new Cmd/Ctrl+C and Cmd/Ctrl+X bindings this PR adds (and that this delta now pins with tests). `docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:146-153` still lists only arrows, Delete/Backspace and Esc as keys handled while an image is selected, so the documented shape of `imageKeyHandler` diverges from the implemented one. Behavior is as specified, so the cost stays inside the codebase; folding two rows into that existing table (not a parallel doc) is the fix.

The originating task doc's acceptance list (docs/tasks/active/20260829-docs-copy-paste-integrity-todo.md:51-62) contains only copy criteria — every image criterion says Cmd/Ctrl+C — yet this delta adds four cut tests (shortcut does not drop selection, Caps Lock variant, writes payload + removes inline, round-trips through paste). Cut is covered by the Plan ("Image-aware copy/cut") so it is not unsanctioned scope, but the acceptance list and the "Review" section (which still describes the branch as one commit plus two review fixes) were not updated for this round, leaving the tested behavior with no stated criterion to check it against.

The cut tests drive the shortcut through `pressCopyShortcut(textarea, 'x')`, whose doc comment and name say "copy shortcut". Since the helper now serves both flavours (matching the `dispatchCopy`/`dispatchCut` split introduced in this same delta), renaming it to something flavour-neutral would keep the test's intent readable.

finding.summary: Cell-aware range traversal re-implemented in the copy path instead of reusing `model/range-slices.ts`, the module that exists specifically to be the single traversal of "which blocks does a DocRange cover"
finding.evidence: `getSelectedBlocks()` now adds its own `layout.blockParentMap.get(start.blockId)` → `resolveNestedTableLayout` → `cell.blocks` → per-block `sliceStart/sliceEnd` walk. `packages/docs/src/model/range-slices.ts:1-17` states it is "The one traversal that decides which text a `DocRange` covers" and was introduced precisely so read and write would not "keep two copies of the dispatch in sync" (issue #715); `visitRangeSlices` (lines 145-226) already implements the identical cross-block-inside-one-cell case (lines 165-190) with the same offset trimming. `TextEditor` holds `this.doc` (line 197) and already imports from this module (`dirtyBlockIdsForRange`, line 23), so reuse was available. The two copies already disagree: `visitRangeSlices` deliberately resolves via `doc.blockParentMap` and gives up on blocks in nested tables, while the new copy path resolves via `layout` + `resolveNestedTableLayout` and covers nested-table cells — so styling and copying can now report different coverage for the same selection, and the third copy must be kept in sync by hand.

verdict.reason: The cell branch exists (text-editor.ts:3747-3755), but the claimed major cost — copy and styling giving "different coverage for the same selection" — is disproved. normalizeRange returns null for any cross-cell/mixed selection (selection.ts:153-171), so the copy branch only serves the both-endpoints-in-one-cell case, which visitRangeSlices already handles at range-slices.ts:165-190 by resolving the table via doc.findBlock (line 172) → findBlockInCells (document.ts:209-238), a recursive chain that DOES resolve nested-table cells; the finding's premise that visitRangeSlices "gives up on blocks in nested tables" is false for this case, so the two cannot disagree. Nor is reuse drop-in: range-slices.ts:16 never reports empty slices and descends into a caught table's cells (211-219), while the copy path must emit empty blocks (text-editor.ts:3783) and clone table blocks whole with tableData (3790-3808), and it needs Block objects rather than (blockId, from, to). The design docs scope the single-traversal invariant to the inline-style read/write pair plus dirty marking (docs-font-controls.md:479-526; docs-nested-tables.md:35-61), not the clipboard. Finally the resolution pattern used is the existing view-layer convention (selection.ts:161-162, text-editor.ts:4044) and the trim loop is the pre-existing shared sliceBlockRange (3766-3813). Residual reuse observation costs nothing outside the codebase's own tidiness → minor, non-blocking.
